COLLEGE NEWS
CCV
Community College of Vermont honored its founding president, Peter Smith, in a celebration held at the Montpelier academic center, where a large meeting space has been renamed the Peter Smith Gathering Place.
CCV was created in 1970 by a special commission charged by then-Gov. Deane Davis to deliver postsecondary education to Vermonters in their local communities. Smith was hired as its first president of CCV.
Today, CCV is the second-largest institution in Vermont, serving more than 10,000 students each year at locations statewide.
Smith’s legacy continues in CCV’s student-centered approach to higher education, which honors learners by meeting them where they are and helping them reach both their educational and career goals. The college mission remains focused on access, particularly for marginalized populations.
‘Across the Fence’
UVM’s “Across the Fence” television show was inducted into Vermont Agricultural Hall of Fame Aug. 27 at the Champlain Valley Expo in Essex Junction.
“Across the Fence” is a 15-minute program broadcast every weekday on WCAX Channel 3 during the noon hour. Co-produced by UVM Extension and WCAX, the program is the only one of its kind in the United States. In February, it celebrated its record-breaking 70th year on the air.
The program informs viewers about the range of work that University of Vermont faculty, staff, and students pursue to address current issues and needs of Vermont and the wider region.
“‘Across the Fence’ has been connecting viewers with agriculture each weekday,” says the Hall of Fame citation. “(Its) stories, information and interviews shaped how agriculture is viewed and appreciated in Vermont. ‘Across the Fence’ has stayed relevant throughout the years by connecting Vermonters to things Vermonters care about, making it uniquely successful in the Green Mountain State over the last seven decades.”
The program is produced by a three-person team led by Senior Producer Keith Silva. He’s joined by Multi-Media Journalist Ben Willis and Associate Producer/Host Amy Finley.
AROUND TOWN
Resilient rivers
MONTPELIER — This fall, North Branch Nature Center presents “Our Resilient Rivers,” free field trips, workshops, and events focused on understanding how rivers and watersheds work.
Vermonters looking to become responsible watershed residents after the 2023/2024 storms can learn about culverts, beavers, dredging, landslides, stormwater, log jams, invasive species, habitat restoration, dams, and making sense of dynamic river channels. Residents get training in river science to better evaluate ideas and decisions to becoming river-resilient communities.
The series kicks off Sept. 20 with RiverFest at NBNC, a festival for all ages comprising field walks, demonstrations, fun activities, music, and games at the water’s edge.
Following events include canoe outings, courses about beaver ecology, tours of flood-altered streams in Montpelier and Plainfield, and workshops about riparian plants, invasive species and river science. Visit northbranchnaturecenter.org/resilientrivers to see the full lineup.
Programs in this series feature presenters from Vermont River Conservancy, Friends of the Winooski River, Montpelier Conservation Commission, Mad River Valley Knotweed Project, Norwich University, Vermont DEC–Rivers Program, Lake Champlain Sea Grant, Intervale Conservation Nursery, and Bonnyvale Environmental Education Center. This series is made possible by grant funding from the Lake Champlain Basin Program and NEIWPCC.
AROUND VT
Memorial service
PITTSFORD — The Vermont Emergency Services Memorial will conduct the annual memorial service recognizing the supreme sacrifice made by 97 Vermonters who have died in the line of duty: firefighters, law enforcement officers, emergency medical service providers, and correctional officers.
The event will be held at 1 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 21, on the grounds of the Vermont Police and Fire Academy, Academy Road, in Pittsford.
Two names will be added to the monument this year to memorialize the line of duty deaths that have occurred in Vermont since the last memorial service.
VTF&W
Bear hunting
The Vermont Fish & Wildlife Department says bear hunting season starts in September and urges hunters to download and read the 2025 Black Bear Hunting Guide from its website.
Vermont has two bear hunting seasons. The early season, Sept. 1 through Nov. 14 requires a special bear tag. Nonresident hunters using dogs cannot start bear hunting until Sept. 15. The late bear season is Nov. 15 through 23. A hunter may only take one bear during the year.
Squirrel hunting
The Vermont hunting season for gray squirrels begins Sept. 1 and continues through Dec. 31, according to Vermont Fish & Wildlife Department.
Tracking dogs
Vermont Fish & Wildlife Department provides a list of certified leashed tracking dog owners who volunteer during the hunting seasons to help hunters locate deer or bear shot during hunting season but not yet recovered. This list, which may be updated during hunting seasons, is available on the VTF&W website.
